title: Claude Code custom pet: Pedalican the pelican
description: Simon accidentally activated Codex Desktop's custom pet feature and created Pedalican - a pelican riding a bicycle. The creation process used GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh and gpt-image-2 across multiple rounds to generate sprite assets. Provides insights into image generation workflows and the open-source implementation.
author: Simon Willison

title: Armin Ronacher on shared language and AI agents
description: Simon quotes Armin Ronacher's insightful analysis of how AI agents affect software engineering. The key insight: before agents, friction in making changes helped synchronize people's understanding of systems. Some of that slowness was waste, but some was the process by which understanding became shared.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Armin Ronacher)

title: Lobsters migration to SQLite completed
description: Community site Lobsters completed migration from MariaDB to SQLite. Results: CPU usage down, memory usage down, site snappier, 1/2 the VPS cost. The site now runs on a single VPS with a 3.8GB primary database, demonstrating that you can get a lot done with single server and SQLite in 2026.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI coding impact on GitHub activity
description: Simon analyzes his GitHub code frequency chart for Datasette, showing a dramatic spike in activity aligned with Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol releases. The data provides concrete illustration of how coding agents and frontier models are impacting developer productivity.
author: Simon Willison

title: DOOMQL: SQLite as game engine
description: Peter Gostev built DOOMQL using GPT-5.6 Sol - a Doom-like game where SQL owns movement, collision, enemies, combat, and every RGB pixel. Simon demonstrates it with Datasette Apps, creating a web interface that shows the game state refreshing from SQL queries.
author: Simon Willison

title: Directly Responsible Individuals (DRI) and AI agents
description: Simon explores the concept of 'Directly Responsible Individuals' in the context of LLM-powered agents. He argues that agents should never be considered DRI for projects - accountability remains uniquely human. References IBM's 1979 training slide about computers never making management decisions.
author: Simon Willison

title: GPT-5.6 family: Luna, Terra, Sol released
description: OpenAI's latest flagship model family with three sizes (Luna, Terra, Sol) hits general availability. Simon Willison provides detailed analysis of the new models, their capabilities, and pricing implications. The release represents another significant step in model capability improvements.
author: Simon Willison

title: Rewriting Bun in Rust with coding agents
description: Jarred Sumner's detailed blog post about rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust using sophisticated agentic engineering. The project used coordinated parallel agents, adversarial code review, and a language-independent test suite. Cost $165,000 in API tokens and resulted in a Rust implementation that's 10% faster on Linux.
author: Simon Willison (analyzing Jarred Sumner)

title: GPT-Live: ChatGPT voice mode upgraded
description: OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT voice mode to GPT-Live, replacing the GPT-4o era model. New model can delegate harder tasks to GPT-5.5 and maintain conversation flow. Simon reports the model is much more useful as a brainstorming partner, though encountered a bug where it interrupted with inappropriate laughter.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI-written change descriptions considered harmful
description: Simon quotes Kenton Varda's decision to declare a moratorium against AI-written change descriptions (PR messages, commits, issues). AI was writing descriptions that outlined code details but omitted higher-level framing needed for review - worse than useless for understanding what code does.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Kenton Varda)

title: sqlite-utils 4.0: Database schema migrations
description: Major release of sqlite-utils 4.0, the first major version bump since 2020. Introduces three major features: database migrations, nested transactions via db.atomic(), and support for compound foreign keys. Simon used Claude Fable 5 extensively in the development process.
author: Simon Willison

title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2: Mostly written by Claude Fable for $149.25
description: Simon experimentally used Claude Fable 5 to help develop sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, costing about $149.25 in API tokens. The experience demonstrated how coding agents can help maintain high standards for major version releases while reducing manual development effort.
author: Simon Willison
